name: Alofaaga Blowholes
note: Natural feature: lava-tube blowholes on the south-west coast near Taga village, where waves throw water up through the rock. Wikivoyage lists it first under See.

name: Peapea Cave
note: Cave: a lava tube about 1 km long near Letui village, with white-rumped swiftlets; a guide is needed to open the locked entrance. Wikipedia spells it Pe'ape'a Cave.

name: Paia Dwarfs Cave
note: Cave: a legendary cave over 1 km long in the north-east near Paia village; exploring it takes most of a day and a guide from Paia is essential.

name: Mount Matavanu Lava Fields
note: Lava fields: barren moonscape from the 1905-1911 eruptions of Mt Matavanu, reached by a roughly three-hour walk from Paia village.

name: Saleaula Lava Field
note: Lava field: flow from the 1905-1911 Matavanu eruptions that buried Saleaula and Salago villages; reached by road from the ferry and a guide is needed for the churches. Fee charged.

name: Afu Aau Falls
note: Waterfall: the most spectacular jungle waterfall on Savaii (Wikivoyage: Olemoe Falls), a half-hour walk from a 4WD track.

name: Pulemelei Mound
note: Historic site: an ancient earthen structure of 60 by 50 m and 12 m high, the largest ancient structure in Polynesia, in Palauli district near Olemoe Falls.

name: Sapapaliʻi
note: Historic village and monument: a plaque and monument where missionary John Williams landed in 1830, the first to bring Christianity to Samoa. Village of the north-east coast.

name: Tafua Peninsula Rainforest Preserve
note: Nature reserve: rainforest with good birdwatching on the south-east peninsula; a walk leads up to the volcanic crater that dominates Tafua.

name: Falealupo Rainforest Preserve
note: Nature reserve: a village-run rainforest preserve on the north-west peninsula with a 25 m canopy walkway and a sleeping platform in the trees.

name: Falealupo
note: Village and peninsula at the westernmost point of Savaii, about 32 km from the dateline; Wikivoyage names the Falealupo Peninsula as a reason to rent a car, and Wikipedia gives its sunset and millennium history.

name: Falealupo Church Ruins
coordinates_source: OpenStreetMap building (Nominatim): Falealupo Catholic Church Ruins
note: Monument: the ruined Catholic church at Falealupo, a landmark described in travel blogs; no Wikipedia article found by the search.

name: Satoalepai Turtle Reserve
note: Wildlife encounter: a turtle reserve on the east coast, 35 minutes from the ferry, where visitors swim with turtles rescued from fishing nets.

name: Aganoa Beach
note: Beach: Savaii's major surfing location on the south coast, with beachfront fales and surf operators; Wikivoyage also names Savaii Surfaris there.

name: Manase
note: Village and beach: the north-coast beach village at Manase, with beach fales, north-coast surf breaks and Raci's Beach Club; Wikivoyage calls the beach the most popular on the island.

name: Fagamalo
note: Village and surf spot on the north-east coast, named by Wikivoyage for north-coast surf (December to April) and as home of the Dive Savaii base.

name: Lesolo
coordinates_source: OpenStreetMap place=locality (Nominatim): Lesolo, Pu'apu'a; surf break location unverified
note: Surf spot on the north coast, named by Wikivoyage among the north-coast breaks (December to April); a surf break rather than a visitor destination.

name: Wreck of the Juno
note: Dive site: the wreck of the Juno, dating from 1881, a popular dive off the Fagamalo/Manase area on the north-east coast.

name: Mataolealelo Spring
note: Natural feature: a freshwater spring near Manase, mentioned by Wikivoyage only in passing beside the Tailua beach fales (a Sleep listing); no entry of its own.

name: Satuiatua
note: Beach and surf spot on the south-west coast with a picturesque beach and good offshore surfing; a village beach, named by Wikipedia and travel blogs.

name: Lano
note: Village and surf break: Wikipedia names reef-break surf off Lano village; no visitor source gives it a stop of its own.

name: Moso's Footprint
note: Natural feature: a rock formation named by Wikipedia among the island's prehistoric geological sites; no visitor source gives it a stop.

name: Silisili
note: Mountain: Mt Silisili, at 1,858 m the highest peak in Samoa (Wikipedia), in the central highlands; no visitor source names a set visit.

name: Mata o le Afi
note: Volcano: a Savaii volcano that erupted in 1902 (Wikipedia), named among the island's recent volcanic features; no visitor source names a stop.

name: Mauga Afi
note: Volcano: a volcanic cone on Savaii whose eruption, dated by Wikipedia to 1725, produced one of the island's lava fields.

name: Central Savaiʻi Rainforest
note: Protected area: about 72,700 ha of rainforest and more than 100 volcanic craters in the central highlands, the largest contiguous rainforest in Polynesia; no visitor infrastructure named. Its Wikipedia title redirects to the island article, so views count as 0; coordinates unresolved (OSM down; the island centre is not its point).

name: Vailoa
note: Archaeological site: prehistoric settlement remains in Palauli district, named by Wikipedia alongside Sapapaliʻi.

name: Safune
note: Village on the central north coast where the 1926 documentary Moana was filmed, with a cave pool used as a film laboratory; a village, with no visitor listing.

name: Salelologa
note: Town: the ferry terminal and only township on Savaii, with a Monday to Saturday market and most services; a gateway with a visitor hub rather than an attraction.
